args.doc: Every sector carrying this tag.
args.name: tag

args.doc: Where the surface ends up. Neighbour targets are resolved AT TRIGGER TIME, because a staircase raised by an earlier trigger changes what 'the next higher floor' means.
args.name: to

args.doc: The height, when `to` is "absolute".
args.name: height

args.doc: Added to the resolved height. A Doom door opens to the lowest neighbouring ceiling less four Doom units, which is to = lowest_neighbour_ceiling with offset = "-0.0834".
args.name: offset

args.doc: Units per tick. Never zero: a door that shut instantly would crush whoever stood under it with no warning.
args.name: speed

args.doc: Defaults to "once". A pingpong crusher needs no further bookkeeping at all -- it is a pure function of the tick, so the client rides it without another message.
args.name: loop

args.doc: Move even if this runtime already has something in flight there. Off by default.
args.name: interrupt

args.doc: The tag that sector carried when this trigger was written. Sector indices come from declaration order, so inserting a sector renumbers the ones after it; this catches that at load. Optional, because addressing a sector by `tag` instead of by index needs no guard at all -- and because "event" and "behind" resolve from the event, so there is nothing to check until one arrives.
args.name: expect_tag

actions.doc: PARAMETRIC sector motion: a start offset, an end offset, a duration. Replicated once and computed by every client for ticks the server has not reached, so a door costs one message and predicts free.

actions.doc: SCRIPTED-DISCRETE motion: whatever this trigger decided, with no closed form. The server streams it in every snapshot and riders fall back to anchor-relative prediction. It costs bandwidth every tick it moves and it costs prediction; reach for sector_move unless you specifically need something no client could derive.
actions.name: sector_offset

args.doc: Which of the event's two handles to act on: the one that DID it (default) or the one it was done to. Ambiguous otherwise, and guessing wrong is silent.
args.name: who

actions.doc: Move the event's entity. Deferred to the tick's flush point like every other mutation, so a trigger that reads the position back in the same callback still sees the old one.

args.doc: Relative. -10 is ten points of damage.
args.name: add

args.doc: Which of the event's two handles to act on: the one that DID it (default) or the one it was done to. Ambiguous otherwise, and guessing wrong is silent.
args.name: who

actions.doc: Health is the server's; the engine has no notion of it and a client only ever learns its own.
actions.name: set_hp

args.doc: Which of the event's two handles to act on: the one that DID it (default) or the one it was done to. Ambiguous otherwise, and guessing wrong is silent.
args.name: who

actions.doc: Whether other bodies collide with the event's entity or prop. A corpse left solid is a wall that appeared where you were about to run.
actions.name: set_solid

args.doc: Which of the event's two handles to act on: the one that DID it (default) or the one it was done to. Ambiguous otherwise, and guessing wrong is silent.
args.name: who

actions.doc: The animation STATE, never a frame and never a duration -- which frame is on screen is the client's decision.
actions.name: set_animation

args.doc: Which of the event's two handles to act on: the one that DID it (default) or the one it was done to. Ambiguous otherwise, and guessing wrong is silent.
args.name: who

actions.doc: Remove the event's prop, or a scripted agent. Refused for a player, loudly: a script cannot delete a person.
actions.name: despawn

actions.doc: By catalogue name. A name the operator has not installed is an error naming the file, not a silent nothing.
actions.name: spawn_prop

actions.doc: An agent nobody is sitting at, with the catalogue's body and speed, moved through the same controller a player is.
actions.name: spawn_enemy

args.doc: A movement parameter name; the table is in core.

args.doc: Omit for permanent.
args.name: ticks

args.name: who

actions.doc: A timed change to the RULES of movement for the event's entity. Travels on the reliable channel with an epoch, not as a snapshot flag, because a client running different physics from the server mispredicts every tick until it is told.
actions.name: add_effect

args.doc: Omit for the next level in the server's progression.
args.name: level

actions.doc: Moves THAT player, and nobody else. Someone still fighting through the level is not yanked along because a faster player found the switch.
actions.name: change_map

args.doc: The key of an entry in the trigger table's `panels`. A panel is a layout, and a layout is data an editor draws -- it is not an argument list.
args.name: panel

actions.doc: Open a panel for the event's entity.
actions.name: ui_open

actions.doc: Close a panel this trigger table opened for the event's entity.
actions.name: ui_close

actions.doc: How the camera follows, for whoever is watching this entity. Never where it is: the camera is the client's, and Lua configures and triggers it only.
actions.name: camera

actions.doc: A transient visual with no identity: a tracer, a flash, an impact. A client that missed one has missed nothing it needs.
actions.name: vfx

args.doc: Defaults to 1.
args.name: by

actions.doc: Per map, not per player. Three switches that between them open one door are a counter and a condition.
actions.name: counter_add

actions.doc: Remember something under a name: a number, a string or a boolean. Where counter_add counts, this NAMES a state -- "open", "locked", true -- which is the thing a counter cannot hold and the thing an author reaches for when a number would be a code.
actions.name: set_property

args.doc: A Lua function taking the event table. Works under every trust profile; an editor cannot round-trip it.
args.name: fn

args.doc: Lua source, compiled once at load with `ev` in scope. An editor can round-trip it; it needs `loadstring`, which Trust::Strict removes.
args.name: code

actions.doc: THE ESCAPE HATCH, and the only place a trigger stops being a bounded vocabulary. Everything else here is a named verb over a binding; this is arbitrary script, with the whole sandbox in reach. Compiled at LOAD, so a syntax error names the trigger instead of surfacing the first time somebody presses the switch. Returning false means it did nothing, which is what `once` spends itself on.
actions.name: lua

actions.doc: Set a counter outright.
actions.name: counter_set

actions.doc: Arm another trigger.
actions.name: enable

actions.doc: Disarm another trigger. A disabled trigger is still dispatched to and still costs its lookup; it just does nothing.
actions.name: disable

actions.doc: Run another trigger's actions NOW, re-checking its conditions and carrying the current event with it. Nesting is bounded: see MAX_RUN_DEPTH in maps/scripts/triggers.lua.
actions.name: run

args.doc: Count the ticks from when this sector's motion settles, rather than from now. A door waits after it has finished opening, not after the button.
args.name: after

args.doc: The tag that sector carried when this trigger was written. Sector indices come from declaration order, so inserting a sector renumbers the ones after it; this catches that at load. Optional, because addressing a sector by `tag` instead of by index needs no guard at all -- and because "event" and "behind" resolve from the event, so there is nothing to check until one arrives.
args.name: expect_tag

actions.doc: The replacement for `wait`, and the only one. Schedules another trigger to run at tick + `ticks`; the runtime drains due timers on on_tick. Nothing suspends, so nothing can be resumed -- see docs/TRIGGERS.md, "No wait".
actions.name: run_after

actions.doc: A line on the server's log, prefixed with the map and the trigger's name. The debugging surface an author actually has: "this switch does nothing" is answerable when the log says which side was reached and which trigger declined it.
actions.name: log

args.doc: The sector index on the other side of that side when this trigger was written, or -1 for a plain wall. REQUIRED -- see below.
args.name: expect_neighbour

conditions.doc:
The event's side index is this one. The commonest condition there is: a switch IS a side index.

`expect_neighbour` is not optional, and it is not ceremony. Side indices come from the order mapc walks the .map, so inserting a single vertex anywhere renumbers every side after it -- and a table full of stale indices loads perfectly and quietly watches the wrong walls. Measured: one added vertex pointed all four of maps/doors_trig.lua's sides at blank wall while the runtime reported '11 triggers on 4 events'. Checked at load, the whole table is refused instead. doom.lua carries the same guard on every converted line, for the same reason.
conditions.name: side_is

Optional, because addressing a sector by `tag` instead of by index needs no guard at all -- and because "event" and "behind" resolve from the event, so there is nothing to check until one arrives.
args.name: expect_tag

conditions.doc: The sector the event named is this one.

args.doc: Which sector to read; defaults to the event's.

conditions.doc: A sector's `tag` is this number. A tag is a number the map carries and nothing else -- what it MEANS is the trigger that reads it.
conditions.name: sector_tag_is

conditions.doc: The event's entity is a person, not a scripted agent. A player is an agent with no catalogue kind: nobody placed it, so it walked in.
conditions.name: entity_is_player

conditions.doc: The event's entity is a catalogue entry of this name ("imp"). By name, so renumbering assets/props.txt cannot silently point this at something else.
conditions.name: entity_kind_is

conditions.doc: The entity is standing in a sector carrying this tag -- which is not the same as the sector the event named.
conditions.name: entity_in_sector_tag

conditions.doc: The thing the event was done TO -- the prop you walked into, what your swing reached -- is this catalogue entry. Props and agents answer the same question, so one condition covers both; a player has no catalogue entry and is never a match.
conditions.name: target_name_is

conditions.doc: The panel event names this widget id, and -- if `value` is given -- carries this value.
conditions.name: widget_is

args.doc: The tag that sector carried when this trigger was written. Sector indices come from declaration order, so inserting a sector renumbers the ones after it; this catches that at load. Optional, because addressing a sector by `tag` instead of by index needs no guard at all -- and because "event" and "behind" resolve from the event, so there is nothing to check until one arrives.
args.name: expect_tag

conditions.doc: Nothing this runtime started on that sector is still in flight. The guard a repeatable door needs: pressing a moving door again must not restart it half-way.
conditions.name: sector_at_rest

args.doc: The tag that sector carried when this trigger was written. Sector indices come from declaration order, so inserting a sector renumbers the ones after it; this catches that at load. Optional, because addressing a sector by `tag` instead of by index needs no guard at all -- and because "event" and "behind" resolve from the event, so there is nothing to check until one arrives.
args.name: expect_tag

conditions.doc: The sector's current vertical offset is at or above `z`. This is how 'the door is open' is asked without the engine having any idea what a door is: the offset is the truth a client also sees, so a flag stored here could disagree with it and this cannot.
conditions.name: sector_offset_at_least

conditions.doc: A named property this trigger table keeps equals this value. The same store counters use, so a counter and a property of one name are one thing rather than two that shadow each other. Compared with `==`, so a property set to the string "open" is not equal to the number 0 and never accidentally matches.
conditions.name: property_is

conditions.doc: A named counter this trigger table keeps is at or above `value`. Counters start at zero and are per map, not per player.
conditions.name: counter_at_least

conditions.doc: Another trigger's enabled flag. Reading it, never writing it -- `enable`/`disable` are the actions.
conditions.name: trigger_enabled

conditions.doc: The world tick is at or past this number. dnp.tick() is the only clock: a trigger that read a wall clock would destroy replay.
conditions.name: tick_at_least

events.doc: Every tick, before the world steps. The runtime always registers this one, whether a map uses it or not, because it is where tick deadlines are drained.
events.name: on_tick

events.doc: Every tick, after the world has stepped and positions are final.
events.name: on_post_tick

events.doc: An entity pressed use while facing a side within reach. `side` is an index; `sector` is the sector the entity was standing in. Edge-triggered: holding the button works a switch once.
events.name: on_interact

events.doc: An entity's movement crossed a side flagged `trigger`. Reported as the side of the sector the entity LEFT, so the two directions across one line are two different side indices and a trip-wire that fires both ways needs both.
events.name: on_cross

events.doc: An entity is standing inside a prop. Reported EVERY TICK the overlap holds -- 'once' is something the trigger does by removing the prop or by setting `once`.
events.name: on_touch

events.doc: An entity pressed use on a prop the catalogue marks `usable`.
events.name: on_prop_use

events.doc: A swing connected. `entity` is the attacker; `target` is an entity or a prop -- ask with entity_kind_is / prop_name_is rather than by comparing numbers.
events.name: on_attack

events.doc: A moving sector closed on an entity. `crush_kind` is "vertical" or "pinned". Reported on the FIRST tick of an episode only.
events.name: on_crush

events.doc: A player worked a widget in a panel a script opened. `value` has already been clamped to what the widget itself declared.
events.name: on_ui_event

widgets.doc: Static text. Sends nothing -- an on_ui_event naming a label did not come from a person, and the server drops it.
widgets.name: label

widgets.doc: Sends 0 or 1. Any other value is clamped to one of those before a trigger sees it.
widgets.name: toggle

widgets.doc: An integer in [lo, hi]. The server clamps to the range the widget itself declared, so a trigger never sees a value this panel could not have produced.
widgets.name: slider

widgets.doc: An index into `options`. An index outside the list is dropped rather than clamped: there is no nearest valid answer.
widgets.name: select
